response.content:
## Companies That Entered the French Market in 2026

Based on available information, several notable companies have entered or announced entry into the French market during 2026:

### Confirmed Market Entries in 2026

- **Celsius Holdings (CELH)** — The U.S. energy-drink maker entered the French market through a strategic alliance with **Suntory Beverage & Food France**, marking a significant step in its international expansion.

- **Lucid Group (LCID)** — The U.S. luxury electric vehicle manufacturer announced its entry into France, with plans to open its first retail and service locations for French buyers (first three sites targeted for early 2027, with 16+ partner locations by end of 2027).

- **innoscripta SE** — The German technology company (ISIN: DE000A40QVM8) successfully entered the French market in the first half of 2026, alongside the UK and the US, signing its first customer contracts. The company reported 43% year-on-year revenue growth in H1 2026.

- **Brantone Veylor** — This financial services firm launched a European strategic expansion identifying France as one of four priority markets (alongside the UK, Romania, and Germany), positioning France as a key market for high-end client services, brand development, and institutional cooperation.

### Announced / Planned Entries (late 2026 into 2027)

- **VEVOR** — The global home improvement brand (serving 30+ million households worldwide) confirmed at IFA Berlin 2026 that it plans to open its **first European store in France in 2027**.

- **OMODA & JAECOO** (Chery Group) — The Chinese automaker brand deepened its European footprint in 2026, with cumulative European sales surpassing 250,000 units across 20 countries, including a French brand launch strategy announced at Auto China 2026.

Despite a challenging macroeconomic backdrop — with Moody's cutting France's 2026 GDP growth forecast to just 0.2% — the country continued to attract foreign companies, particularly in beverages, electric vehicles, technology, and financial services.

context.content: # Why Is Lucid Group (LCID) Entering France A Big Test Of Its Growth Story? * Lucid Group (NasdaqGS:LCID) announced its entry into France with its first retail and service locations for French buyers. * The move brings Lucid's award-winning models, including the World Luxury Car of the Year, directly into a new European market. * Lucid's decision to build out French showrooms and service hubs is only one piece of what is changing for the business today. The French retail and service rollout lines up with Lucid Group's push to turn technology leadership and partnerships into a broader international footprint. It reinforces the part of the Narrative that leans on brand and product differentiation, especially as buyers can directly compare Lucid Gravity and Air against premium EVs from Tesla and Mercedes in a mature market. The takeaway is that the same French expansion can support a bullish or cautious view on Lucid Group, depending on which part of the Narrative you think is stronger right now.

context.content: # Lucid Expands in France to Boost Customer Reach Amid Uneven Sales. **Lucid Group, Inc.** LCID plans to expand its European presence by opening its first retail and service locations in France in the first quarter of 2027. The locations will support vehicle sales and after-sales service, allowing customers to explore and order its Lucid Air sedan and Lucid Gravity SUV. The initiative marks another step in Lucid's strategy of combining its direct-to-consumer model with partnerships to expand its retail and service footprint in Europe. By expanding its retail and service network in France, Lucid aims to broaden customer access to its vehicles, strengthen its local market presence and support its efforts to grow its European business. Its earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in three of the trailing four quarters and missed once, with the average earnings surprise being 8.6%. Its earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in two of the trailing four quarters and missed twice, with the average negative surprise being 13.7%.

context.content: **Coordinated Development Across Four Core Markets—the United Kingdom, France, Romania, and Germany—Marks a New Stage of International Growth**. Brantone Veylor recently announced the launch of a new phase in its European market strategy, identifying the United Kingdom, France, Romania, and Germany as four priority markets for its European business development. Through differentiated positioning across the four core markets, the company aims to strengthen its capabilities in international capital market connectivity, institutional cooperation, regional operations, financial technology support, and global client services. Brantone Veylor plans to position the United Kingdom as a strategic hub connecting the company's global business operations, international capital resources, and European markets. By drawing on the United Kingdom's mature financial services ecosystem, international business environment, English-language market advantages, and broad global client base, the company seeks to improve its connectivity with international capital markets, professional institutions, and global investors, while establishing a stronger foundation for its continued expansion across Europe. France will serve as one of Brantone Veylor's key European markets for high-end client services, brand development, and institutional cooperation.

context.content:
Even though it maintained its Aa3-Negative rating in late October, Moody's said in a report to clients Tuesday that "political uncertainty, higher bond yields and fiscal challenges have constrained growth in 2026".

The new outlook is below the government's own target of 0.5 percent, and comes as the Bank of France recently lowered its own forecast to 0.3 percent.

International investors are increasingly concerned about French public debt that stands at around 120 percent of GDP -- one of the highest levels in the eurozone and well above the EU limit of 60 percent.

At the same time, the country is facing fierce protests denouncing the surging cost of living and demanding higher spending on education and other public services. [...] AFP

# France 2026 growth forecast cut to 0.2% by Moody's

By AFP

Published on November 11, 2026 at 14:43

  X
  LinkedIn
  Facebook

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is struggling to get a deficit-cutting budget through the French parliament — Kenzo TRIBOUILLARD / AFP

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is struggling to get a deficit-cutting budget through the French parliament — Kenzo TRIBOUILLARD / AFP

Credit rating agency Moody's has halved its full-year GDP growth forecast for France to 0.2 percent, two weeks after reiterating its negative outlook as the government struggles to cut its debt pile. [...] Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is struggling to pass a deficit-cutting budget for 2027 in a Parliament where President Emmanuel Macron's centrists no longer hold a majority.

In a bid to defuse the protests, Lecornu said Monday that the minimum wage would be raised 1.6 percent to around 1,502 euros net a month -- far below union demands.

"This political instability, also visible in the current social tensions, risks hampering the French government's ability to address key policy challenges such as an elevated fiscal deficit, rising debt burden, and increase in borrowing costs," Moody's said in its October 27 report.

The French economy shrank 0.1 percent in the third quarter after stagnating in the second quarter, putting the country on the brink of recession.
